correctness.rationale: For the infinite bilateral map the character pullback is multiplication by P^n on Laurent polynomials and is injective. A compact image subgroup is determined by its annihilator; its index is 2 to the dimension of support-S multiples of P^n, and changing pinned bits only translates the coset. At a primitive cube root alpha, a binomial vanishes exactly for equal residues and the trinomial exactly for three distinct residues. Removing the common dyadic power of the differences leaves a simple root in either case: in the normalized trinomial the derivative is either a monomial or two distinct powers of alpha. Thus each eligible sparse sum has the asserted exact survival clock, including n equal to its threshold. In the equal-residue case the binomials span the even-parity plane until the shared minimum clock and only the unique maximum survives thereafter; all other cases have at most one relation. At time zero a pinned cylinder is proper. A surviving triple of clock h has span at least 2h, while an eligible pair of clock h has gap at least 3h. The scaled triple {0,h,2h} has all residues distinct and its trinomial is P^h, proving both sharpness and lack of any pairwise obstruction. An independent check used the invertible endpoint recurrence for the kernel of F^n: any length-2n seed extends uniquely to a bilateral kernel element, and the image codimension is 3 minus the rank of its evaluation on the pins. Python /workspace/rule150_recurrence_reproduction.py verified 296400 triple/time pairs and extrema through span 96; this corroborates but does not replace the proof. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.

Its written scope starts at degree three, but inspection of its full decisive proof shows that the restriction is not used: degree two needs only the elementary identity among the three nonzero elements of F4 and the obvious span of P itself. The Rule 150 statement is a mechanical specialization of the proof, not a distinct scientific result. This is statement-and-proof coverage, not a priority or in-scope citation claim.
